name: Greek Turkey Spanakorizo Skillet
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7.75 oz (220 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Thaw the frozen spinach and squeeze it dry, hard, with your hands or in a clean towel. Wet spinach makes soggy rice, and this is the step people skip and then regret.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet and cook the diced onion until soft, about 8 minutes, then add the garlic for one minute.
Add the ground turkey and brown it, breaking it up as it goes, until it is cooked through to 165F with no pink left.
Stir in the tomato paste and let it darken for a minute, then add the squeezed spinach, the dried dill, salt, and black pepper.
Add the rinsed rice and enough water to cover it by about half an inch, bring it to a boil, then drop to low, cover, and cook 18 to 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Kill the heat, pour in the lemon juice, scatter the chopped fresh mint over the top, and let it sit covered 10 minutes so the rice finishes steaming.
Fluff it with a fork, move it into your weighed pot, and hold the feta back for the containers.

name: Greek Turkey Youvarlakia (Egg-Lemon Meatball and Rice)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the ground turkey with the uncooked rice, grated onion, the dried dill, salt, and black pepper. The rice goes in raw and cooks inside the meatball, which is the whole idea.
Roll the mixture into meatballs and set them aside. Do not pack them tight, since the rice needs room to swell.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot, soften the remaining diced onion and the grated carrot for 6 minutes, then add water to make a light broth and bring it to a simmer.
Lower the meatballs in gently, cover, and simmer 40 minutes until the rice inside is tender and the meat is cooked through to 165F. Do not stir hard, just shake the pot.

Make the avgolemono: whisk the eggs until frothy, whisk in the lemon juice, then ladle in hot broth one spoon at a time while whisking constantly. This tempering step is the only part that can go wrong, so go slow.
Pour the sauce back into the pot off the heat and swirl the pot to combine. Never let it boil again, because boiling scrambles the eggs and there is no undo.
Scatter the chopped fresh herb over the top, then move everything into your weighed pot.

name: Green Chile Ground Turkey Skillet
ingredients: Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 3.5 cans (396 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 3.5 cans (892 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (866 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 21 oz (593 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in your biggest skillet or pot. Cook the diced red onion and bell pepper until soft, about 6 minutes, then add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground turkey and break it up as it browns. Cook to 165F with no pink remaining, then stir in the chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Stir in the green chiles, salsa verde, drained black beans, and drained corn. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes so the flavors settle in.
Scatter the cheese over the top, cover, and let it melt for 2 to 3 minutes. Finish with lime juice and chopped cilantro.
Portion the rice into 14 containers and top each with an even share of the skillet.

name: Grilled Pork Tenderloin Burrito Bowl
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 15.25 oz (435 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the tenderloins dry and rub them all over with most of the taco seasoning, salt, and black pepper.
Grill over medium-high heat, or sear in a hot pan and finish in a 400F oven, until the thickest part reads 145F, about 15 to 20 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, then dice and toss with the BBQ sauce.
While the pork cooks, simmer the rice in the chicken broth with the diced yellow onion, covered, until tender.
Make the salsa: drain the diced tomatoes well, then stir them with minced jalapeno, diced red onion, lime juice, chopped cilantro, and a pinch of taco seasoning.
Portion rice into 14 containers, then divide the BBQ pork, salsa, and shredded cheddar on top.

name: Ground Beef and Broccoli Bowls
ingredients: Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain any excess fat.
Steam or microwave the broccoli florets until bright green and just tender.
Whisk the soy sauce, beef broth, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch into a quick sauce.
Pour the sauce over the beef and simmer until it thickens and glossy-coats the meat.
Fold in the broccoli, then serve everything over cooked rice in each container.

name: Ground Beef Baked Gnocchi
ingredients: Potato Gnocchi (Great Value): 68 oz dry (1930 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 7 oz (198 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F. In a big oven-safe pot, brown the ground beef with the diced onion, breaking it up as it cooks, until no pink remains.
Add the garlic and Italian seasoning and cook 1 minute, then season with salt and black pepper.
Pour in the marinara sauce with a splash of water, bring it to a simmer, and stir in the uncooked gnocchi. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes, stirring so nothing sticks.
Dollop the ricotta over the top and scatter on the mozzarella.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until the cheese is melted and the sauce bubbles at the edges. Rest 5 minutes.
Portion evenly into 14 containers.

name: Ground Beef Fried Rice Bowls
ingredients: Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (6 g)
steps: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Toss in the peas and carrots and cook until they warm through.
Add the cooked rice, ideally day-old and cold, so it fries up instead of turning mushy.
Drizzle in the soy sauce and sesame oil with the garlic and ginger, stirring until everything is coated.
Push it around the hot skillet a couple minutes to get that fried-rice edge, then portion out.

name: Ground Beef Gyro Bowls
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 1/4 cup crumbled (tzatziki) (113 g)
Salt (Morton): 1 tsp meat + 1/2 tsp tzatziki (20 g)
steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, cumin, garlic powder, and onion powder, then drain.
Cook the rice separately so it stays fluffy.
Stir the fresh garlic and a scoop of the greek yogurt into the beef for a creamy finish.
Whisk the rest of the greek yogurt with a little garlic for a quick tzatziki-style sauce.
Layer beef and green peppers over rice, then spoon the yogurt sauce on top.

name: Ground Beef Shawarma Bowls
steps: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, cumin, paprika, garlic, and garlic powder, then drain.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and beef broth and simmer until saucy.
Cook the rice separately so it stays light and fluffy.
Whisk the greek yogurt with a little garlic for a quick cooling sauce.
Spoon the shawarma beef over rice and finish with the yogurt drizzle.

name: Ground Beef Stroganoff Pasta
ingredients: Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion and a pat of butter, then drain.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and shrink down.
Boil the rotini separately until just tender, then drain.
Pour in the beef broth and dijon, simmer, then stir in the light sour cream off the heat so it stays smooth.
Fold the cooked rotini into the creamy sauce and portion it out.

name: Ground Beef Teriyaki Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/4 tsp (2 g)
steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Steam the broccoli florets and sliced red bell pepper until crisp-tender.
Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, honey, beef broth, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch into a glaze.
Pour the glaze over the beef and simmer until it thickens and coats the meat.
Serve the teriyaki beef and veggies over rice in each container.

name: Ground Turkey Broccoli Cheddar Rice Skillet
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 16.75 oz (475 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat most of the olive oil in your biggest pot. Brown the ground turkey, breaking it up, until it reaches 165F with no pink remaining. Add the onion and cook until soft, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the rinsed rice, chicken broth, oregano, basil, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes until the rice is nearly tender.
Stir in the milk, Dijon mustard, and broccoli florets. Cover and cook 5 more minutes until the broccoli is bright and tender.
Pull the pot off the heat and stir in the cheddar a handful at a time until the whole thing turns creamy.
In a small skillet, toast the bread crumbs in the butter until golden, then stir in the parmesan.
Portion into 14 containers and sprinkle the crumb topping over each so it stays crisp.

name: Ground Turkey Burrito Bowl
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 2.5 cans (632 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 7.25 oz (208 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in your biggest skillet. Cook the diced red onion and green bell peppers until soft, about 6 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the ground turkey and break it up as it browns. Cook to 165F with no pink remaining, then stir in the taco seasoning, salt, and black pepper.
Pour in the salsa and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens into a saucy taco filling.
Stir in the drained black beans and heat through.
Portion rice into 14 containers, top with the turkey mixture, then finish with cheese and chopped cilantro.

name: Ground Turkey Calabacitas Skillet
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 1.8 cans (452 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 1 can (433 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground turkey in your largest skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into crumbles and letting it take on real color before you stir it around.
Add the diced onion and the minced jalapeno and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic and the ground cumin for one more minute.
Push everything to the side, add the tomato paste to the bare part of the pan, and let it cook against the metal for two minutes until it darkens and loses its tinny edge.
Add the diced zucchini and cook 6 to 8 minutes over high heat. Keep the pan hot so the squash browns rather than releasing water and boiling itself.
Stir in the canned diced tomatoes, the drained corn, and the drained black beans, then season with salt and black pepper and simmer 10 minutes to bring it together.
Cook the rice separately while the skillet simmers, so the grains stay distinct instead of soaking up all the sauce.
Taste for salt, then fold in the chopped fresh cilantro off the heat and serve the calabacitas over the rice.

name: Ground Turkey Enchilada Skillet Bowls
ingredients: Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 4 cans (900 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 3 cans (900 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (500 g)
Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 1 can (60 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 bag (168 g)
steps: Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet, then drain any excess liquid.
Stir in the enchilada sauce and the chopped chipotle in adobo for a smoky kick.
Add the black beans and corn and let it all simmer together.
Fold in the cooked rice and stir until everything is warm and coated.
Top with shredded cheddar, cover for a minute to melt it, then dish into bowls.

name: Ground Turkey Lasagna Casserole
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 3.75 tbsp (20 g)
Pasta Shells - jumbo (Great Value): 22.25 oz dry (633 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 9.75 oz (278 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the jumbo shells to just under done, about 2 minutes short of the box time, then drain them. They finish in the oven and overcooked pasta in a bake turns to paste.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot, cook the diced onion 5 minutes, add the garlic for a minute, then brown the ground turkey until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the marinara sauce, the chicken broth, the italian seasoning, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper, and simmer 10 minutes so it thickens up.
Stir the ricotta together with the eggs and the parmesan in a separate bowl. The egg is what keeps the ricotta from weeping water into your casserole.
Fold the drained shells into the meat sauce, then dollop the ricotta mixture through it and stir just twice so you get ribbons of white instead of a uniform pink.
Spread it in your baking pans, cover with the mozzarella, and bake at 375F for 30 minutes until it bubbles at the edges and the cheese browns in spots.
Let it rest 15 minutes, cook the rice, and move the rice into your weighed pot.

name: Ground Turkey Lo Mein
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 24 oz dry (681 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the sauce: honey, soy sauce, sriracha, hoisin, and ground ginger. Set it by the stove.
Boil the lo mein noodles 1 minute short of the package time, drain, and rinse briefly so they do not clump.
Heat half the olive oil in your biggest pot or wok. Brown the ground turkey, breaking it up, until it reaches 165F with no pink remaining. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and stir fry the carrots, onion, bell pepper, and mushrooms until they just soften, about 5 minutes. Add the cabbage and spinach and cook 2 more minutes.
Return the turkey, add the noodles and sauce, and toss over high heat until everything is coated and glossy.
Portion evenly into 14 containers.

name: Ground Turkey Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: Cream of Chicken Soup (generic condensed (USDA)): 3.4 cans (1008 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and chunk the potatoes, cover them with cold salted water, and boil until a fork slides through with no resistance, about 20 minutes.
While the potatoes cook, heat the olive oil in your largest skillet over medium-high and brown the ground turkey, breaking it apart as it goes.
Add the diced onion and the garlic to the turkey, cook 5 minutes until soft, then season with salt, black pepper, and dried thyme.
Stir in the condensed cream of chicken soup and the frozen peas, let it bubble 3 minutes, then spread the filling into a greased 9x13 pan.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Keep them thick. Whipped potatoes will slide right off the filling.
Spoon the mashed potatoes over the filling and spread them to the edges so the pan is sealed, then drag a fork across the top to make ridges that will brown.
Scatter the parmesan over the potatoes and bake at 400F for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is browned and the edges are bubbling. Rest 15 minutes before you portion.

name: Ground Turkey Stir Fry Bowls
ingredients: Yellow Onion: 1 medium sweet onion, diced (385 g)
Green Onions: 3, green parts sliced (90 g)
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Add the sliced zucchini and green peppers and stir fry until they are just tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, teriyaki sauce, honey, and a dash of hot sauce.
Let it bubble a couple minutes so the sauce coats everything and thickens slightly.
Serve it hot over cooked white rice.

name: Ground Turkey Sweet Potato Bowl
ingredients: Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 4.25 oz (118 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Scrub and dice the sweet potatoes into half-inch cubes, toss with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper, and spread on sheet pans.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, flipping once, until browned at the edges and tender in the middle.
While they roast, brown the ground turkey in a big skillet, breaking it up, until it reaches 165F with no pink remaining.
Stir the taco seasoning into the turkey, then pour in the salsa and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until saucy.
Portion the roasted sweet potatoes into 14 containers and top with the turkey mixture.
Finish each with a spoon of light sour cream, a sprinkle of cheese, and chopped cilantro.

name: Gyudon (Japanese Beef and Onion Rice Bowls)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Put the steak in the freezer for 30 to 45 minutes until it is firm but not frozen solid, then slice it against the grain as thin as your knife will allow.
Start the rice so it finishes about when the beef does.
Combine the chicken broth, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar in a wide skillet and bring it to a simmer. Taste it. That broth is what the whole bowl tastes like, so adjust the sugar and soy now.
Add the sliced onions and simmer them for 5 to 7 minutes until they turn soft and translucent.

Lay the beef into the simmering broth in batches, separating the slices as you go, and cook just until the pink disappears. Two minutes is plenty. Overcooked gyudon beef goes tough and stringy, and there is no coming back from it.
Skim any foam off the top, season with a little salt and pepper, and scatter the sliced green onions over the pan.
Let it sit off the heat for five minutes so the beef soaks up the broth before you portion.

name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 4.25 lb (1890 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Bring a big pot of chicken broth to a bare simmer with a few smashed ginger slices and green onion tops. It should barely move, with a bubble breaking every second or two. A rolling boil makes chicken rubbery.

Lower the chicken breasts in and poach gently until just cooked through, about 15 minutes depending on thickness. Pull them out and drop them straight into ice water for 5 minutes, which stops the cooking and firms up the texture.
Skim the fat off the top of the broth and reserve every drop of the liquid.
Melt the butter with some of the vegetable oil in a pot, fry the minced garlic and ginger until fragrant, add the rinsed rice, and toast it for two minutes.
Pour in the reserved poaching broth, bring it to a boil, then cover and cook on low until the rice is done, about 18 minutes. Rest it covered for 10 minutes more.

Make the sauces while the rice cooks. Blend the rest of the ginger and garlic with the remaining vegetable oil, salt, and lime juice for the ginger garlic sauce, and stir the soy sauce with the sugar for the dark sauce. Blend the jalapeno with a little of each for the chili sauce.
Slice the chilled chicken thick across the grain.

name: Haitian Poulet en Sauce
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.75 lb (3500 g)
Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 7 tbsp (105 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Wash the chicken thighs in a bowl of water with the lemon juice and apple cider vinegar, rubbing the pieces and then draining them well. This citrus wash is a real step in Haitian cooking, not a superstition, and it sets up the flavor.

Make the epis: blend the fresh cilantro, garlic, green bell pepper, dried thyme, black pepper and salt with a splash of the lemon juice until it is a coarse green paste. Rub it into the chicken and refrigerate at least four hours or overnight.
Scrape the marinade off the chicken and reserve it. Heat a large heavy pot over medium-high and brown the thighs in batches until they take color, then set them aside.
Add the diced onion to the pot and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and the reserved epis and cook 3 minutes until the paste turns brick red.
Add water or broth to loosen the sauce, scrape the bottom clean, and return the chicken with its juices. Cover and simmer 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is tender and reads 165F.
While it braises, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes. Toast the peanuts in a dry skillet until they smell nutty, then chop them coarsely.
Chop the chicken, fold the rice through the sauce, and scatter the toasted chopped peanuts over the top for crunch.

name: Halal Cart Chicken and Rice
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.75 lb (2117 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Marinate the chicken: whisk the olive oil, white vinegar, minced garlic, ground coriander, paprika, ground cumin, onion powder, salt and black pepper, then turn the thighs in it and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.

Heat the oven to 450F. Spread the chicken in a single layer on sheet pans and roast 20 to 25 minutes, running the broiler at the end until the edges char in spots. Let it rest, then chop it into rough bite-size pieces on a cutting board, cart style.

Make the turmeric rice: toast the rice in a little oil with the ground turmeric, ground cinnamon and garam masala for two minutes, then add the chicken broth, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low 18 to 20 minutes. Rest it covered another 10 minutes and fluff.

Make the white sauce: whisk the greek yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, a little of the white vinegar, salt and black pepper until smooth. Refrigerate it, because it is better cold and it tightens as it sits.
Dice the cucumber and drain the canned tomatoes well, then toss them with the diced red onion into a quick salad.
Layer the chopped chicken and rice together in your mixing pot so the chicken juices get into the grains.
Keep the white sauce, the hot sauce and the cucumber salad in separate containers so nothing goes soggy in the fridge.

name: Haluski and Kielbasa (Cabbage and Egg Noodles)
ingredients: Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 36.25 oz dry (1026 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Core the cabbage and slice it into thin ribbons. Slice the onion thin as well.
Boil the egg noodles in well salted water until just barely tender, then drain them and set them aside.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins and brown them in a dry skillet until the edges char a little, then move them to a plate.
Melt the butter in that same skillet and cook the onion until it turns soft and translucent.
Add the cabbage in batches, letting each addition wilt down before you add more. Cook it slowly until it goes golden and sweet. Rushing this is the one mistake people make.
Season with salt and black pepper, then return the sausage to the pan and stir it through.
Fold the drained noodles into the cabbage and sausage in your big pot until everything is coated in butter.

name: Ham and Potato Cheddar Casserole
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 18.25 oz (519 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and slice the potatoes thin and even, about the thickness of a coin, so they cook through at the same rate.
Melt the butter in a large pot, stir in the flour, and cook the paste for a minute so it loses its raw taste.
Whisk in the milk and chicken broth a little at a time until the sauce is smooth and thickened, then stir in the diced yellow onion.
Take the pot off the heat, add most of the shredded cheddar, and stir until it melts. Adding cheese off the heat keeps the sauce from breaking.
Fold in the diced ham, the sliced potatoes, and the frozen peas, and season with salt and black pepper.
Spread everything into a large baking dish, cover with foil, and bake at 375 degrees until a knife slides through the potatoes with no resistance.
Uncover, scatter the remaining cheddar over the top, and bake until browned and bubbling, then let it rest fifteen minutes before portioning.

name: Ham and White Bean Soup
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, carrots and celery, and drain and rinse the white beans.
Heat a large pot and cook the diced ham until the edges brown and it renders a little fat. Browning the ham first is what gives this soup its backbone.
Add the onion, carrots and celery to the pot and cook until they soften and pick up the browned bits.
Stir in the chili powder, dried parsley, black pepper and bay leaves and cook for a minute.
Pour in the chicken broth and the diced tomatoes and bring everything up to a simmer.
Add the drained white beans and simmer gently, mashing a scoop of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth naturally.
Pull the bay leaves, taste for salt, and cook the rice separately to serve it under the soup.

name: Ham Fried Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice the day before if you can and spread it on a sheet pan to cool and dry in the fridge overnight.
Dice the carrots small, slice the green onions and separate the white parts from the green tops, and mince the garlic.
Beat the eggs, then scramble them in a little of the vegetable oil in your largest skillet until just set. Take them out and chop them roughly.
Add more oil and fry the diced ham until the edges crisp, then add the carrots and the white parts of the green onions and cook until the carrots soften.
Add the garlic for a few seconds, then add the cold rice and press it into the hot pan. Let it sit undisturbed between stirs so it toasts instead of steaming.
Pour the soy sauce around the edges of the pan rather than into the middle so it hits hot metal and caramelizes.
Kill the heat, fold in the scrambled egg and the green onion tops, then finish with the sesame oil and black pepper.

name: Harissa Chicken Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1667 g)
Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7.5 oz (210 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Cube the chicken breast and toss it with the harissa paste, a third of the lime juice, salt, garlic powder, cumin, and onion powder.
Sear the chicken in a hot skillet in batches, 6 to 8 minutes per batch, until it reaches 165F inside. Crowding the pan steams it, so give it room.
Whisk the tahini, Greek yogurt, remaining lime juice, and a splash of water into a pourable sauce. Season with salt.
Warm the frozen peas, and dice the cucumber and red onion.
Portion rice into 14 containers, add chicken and peas, then top with cucumber, red onion, feta, and the tahini sauce kept to one side.

name: Hawaiian Loco Moco Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Form the ground beef into 14 thin patties and season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Sear the patties in the olive oil in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through with no pink in the center. Set aside, leaving the drippings.
Make the gravy in the same pan: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the beef broth and soy sauce and simmer until it coats a spoon.
Fry the eggs in a nonstick pan until the whites are set.
Portion rice into 14 containers, add a patty, ladle gravy over, and top each with a fried egg and sliced green onions.

name: High-Protein Turkey Burger Bowl
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 1.25 tbsp (18 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 14.75 oz (415 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Dice the potatoes, toss with a little oil, salt, and paprika, and roast 30 to 35 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Brown the ground turkey in a big skillet, breaking it up, until it reaches 165F with no pink remaining. Season with the Worcestershire, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Whisk the burger sauce: Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, ketchup, Dijon, honey, apple cider vinegar, and finely chopped dill pickles.
Shred the cabbage, halve the cherry tomatoes, and dice the yellow onion.
Portion potatoes and turkey into 14 containers, then top with cabbage, tomatoes, onion, cheddar, and extra pickles.
Keep the sauce in a corner of each box or in small cups and add it after reheating so the crunch survives.

name: Honey Garlic Steak Bites and Potatoes
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (2 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the sirloin into even bite sized cubes and season them with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Sear the cubes in the vegetable oil in batches over high heat, just long enough to brown the outside. They should still be rare in the middle.
Move the seared beef to the slow cooker with any browned bits from the pan.
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, and minced garlic together and pour it over the beef.
Cover and cook on low for 3 hours, until the cubes are tender but still holding their shape.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little cold water, stir it in, and cook on high 15 minutes until the glaze coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the butter off the heat so the glaze goes glossy, then taste for salt.

name: Hong Kong-Style Baked Pork Chop Rice
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 3.5 tbsp (63 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 10.5 oz (298 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice, ideally ahead so it can chill. Pound the pork chops to an even half inch and marinate 15 minutes with the soy sauce, oyster sauce, a little sugar, five-spice powder, salt, and pepper.
Scramble the eggs in butter in your biggest pan, add the rice, and toss over high heat until every grain is coated. Spread the fried rice into baking dishes.
Dredge the chops in the flour, shaking off the extra, and pan fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and 145F inside. Lay them over the rice.
In the same pan, soften the onion and carrots, then add the ketchup, crushed tomatoes, remaining sugar, and a splash of chicken broth. Simmer 5 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the chops, scatter the cheese on top, and bake at 400F until melted and bubbling, 10 to 15 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, then portion into 14 containers.

name: Horseradish Pot Roast Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry, season it with salt, black pepper, and oregano, and sear it in the vegetable oil until it is well browned all over.
Move the roast to the slow cooker and scatter the chopped onion around it.
Whisk the horseradish sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and beef broth together and pour it over the roast.
Cover and cook on low for 7 hours.
Add the sliced mushrooms in the last hour so they hold some texture instead of dissolving.
Shred the beef in the cooker with two forks and stir it through the horseradish gravy.
Cook the rice separately and taste the gravy for salt before you portion.

name: Hungarian Beef Goulash
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the chuck into large cubes, pat them dry, and season with salt and pepper. Brown them in the olive oil over medium-high heat in batches, then set the meat aside. A crowded pot steams instead of searing, and the searing is where the flavor comes from.
Drop the butter into the same pot, add the sliced onions, and cook them low and slow until they collapse and turn golden, about 15 minutes. Stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Pull the pot off the burner and stir in all the paprika. This is the one step people get wrong. Paprika scorches in seconds over direct heat and turns bitter, and there is no fixing it after that.
Return the beef, then add the diced tomatoes, chopped green peppers, caraway seeds, bay leaves, and enough chicken broth to nearly cover everything. Bring it up to a bare simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, stirring every half hour, until a fork slides through the beef with no argument.
Add the carrots and potatoes in big chunks and simmer uncovered another 30 to 40 minutes, until they are tender and the sauce has tightened up. Fish out the bay leaves.
Taste for salt, then let the pot sit off the heat for 10 minutes before you portion it.

name: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.5 lb (3360 g)
Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 26.5 oz dry (750 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks, season with salt and half the black pepper, and toss in the flour until coated.
Brown the chicken in the butter in batches in your biggest pot, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Do not cook it through yet; set it aside.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot until soft, add the garlic, then pull the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika and cayenne so they bloom without burning.
Stir in the tomato paste, sugar, and crushed tomatoes, return the chicken, and simmer covered 20 to 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165F and is tender.
Boil the egg noodles, drain, and divide them among 14 containers.
Off the heat, temper the sour cream with a ladle of hot sauce, stir it back in with the lemon juice, and ladle the paprikash over the noodles.

name: Hungarian Pork and Potato Goulash (Porkolt)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into stew sized cubes. Dice the onions, slice the carrots, chop the red bell peppers and cube the potatoes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and cook the onions slowly until they collapse and go golden. Do not rush this. The onions are your thickener and your sweetness both.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika, oregano and italian seasoning. Off heat is not a suggestion, because paprika burns in seconds and turns bitter.
Put the pot back on the burner, add the pork cubes, and stir until they lose their raw color and take on the paprika.
Add the carrots, red peppers, bay leaves, salt and black pepper, then pour in the chicken broth.
Cover and simmer low until the pork is nearly tender, stirring occasionally so nothing catches on the bottom.
Add the cubed potatoes and cook until they are soft and the sauce has thickened, then fish out the bay leaves.

name: Hunter's Chicken (BBQ Bacon Cheese Bake)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.75 lb (336 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 6.25 oz (175 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 6.25 oz (175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F. Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper and wrap each one in bacon, tucking the ends underneath so they do not unravel in the oven.

Sear the wrapped chicken in a hot dry pan for 2 minutes a side to start rendering the bacon fat. Bacon that goes straight into the oven wrapped around chicken comes out pale and flabby, and this step is the fix.
Arrange the chicken in a large baking dish and brush a generous coat of barbecue sauce over the top of each piece.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165F in the thickest part.
Scatter the shredded cheddar and mozzarella over the top and return it to the oven for 5 to 8 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling at the edges.
While the chicken bakes, cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with salt and pepper, and roast them on a separate sheet pan until crisp.
Steam or roast the green beans just until tender and still green, then let everything rest 5 minutes before packing.

name: Indian Keema Matar (Ground Beef & Peas Curry) Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in your biggest pot and cook the sliced onions until deeply golden, 12 to 15 minutes. This browning is where keema gets its flavor, so take your time.
Add the garlic, ginger, and minced jalapeno and cook 2 minutes, then stir in the cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric, and salt for 30 seconds.
Add the ground beef and break it up as it browns until no pink remains.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and Greek yogurt and simmer uncovered 15 minutes until the mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Stir in the peas and garam masala, simmer 5 minutes, and season with black pepper.
Portion rice into 14 containers and top with an even share of the keema.

name: Indian Turkey Kofta Meatball Curry
ingredients: Red Curry Paste (Thai Kitchen): 7 tbsp (105 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the ground turkey with the eggs, the flour, about a third of the minced garlic, the grated ginger, salt, and black pepper. Mix it just until it holds and stop there.
Roll the mixture into meatballs, set them on oiled sheet pans, and bake at 400F for 18 to 20 minutes until they are browned and cooked through to 165F.
While they bake, heat the olive oil in a wide pot and cook the diced onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden at the edges.
Add the rest of the garlic with the red curry paste and fry it for 2 minutes, until the paste darkens and the kitchen tells you it is ready.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring it to a low simmer, and add the sliced zucchini. Cook 8 minutes until the zucchini is just tender and still holding its shape.
Slide the baked meatballs into the curry and simmer 5 minutes so they soak up the sauce. Taste for salt.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and keep the curry in its own pot for portioning.

name: Indonesian Babi Kecap Pork Rice Bowls
ingredients: Sweet Soy Sauce (ABC (Kecap Manis)): 4 oz (112 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into large cubes, roughly bite and a half sized, since they shrink as they braise.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and brown the pork in batches, giving each piece room so it sears instead of steams.
Add the garlic, ginger, sliced red onion, and dried arbol chiles and cook until fragrant.
Return all the pork, pour in the sweet soy sauce and soy sauce, and add enough water to come most of the way up the meat.
Stir in the ground coriander and ground cloves, bring it to a bare simmer, cover, and cook low and slow until the pork is fork tender.
Uncover and let the liquid reduce until it turns dark, thick, and glossy enough to coat the meat, then season with salt and black pepper.
Cook the rice according to the package while the sauce reduces.

name: Irish Beef and Guinness Stew
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 1 lb (397 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and render it slowly in the pot until it is crisp, then lift it out and leave the fat behind.
Cut the chuck into large cubes, pat them dry, season with salt and black pepper, and brown them hard in the bacon fat and olive oil in batches.
Cook the chopped onion and garlic in the same pot until soft, scraping the bottom clean.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth and chicken broth, and add a can of stout here if you are using it. Add the bay leaves and thyme.
Return the beef and bacon, cover, and simmer very low for 2.5 hours, until the beef surrenders completely.
Add the carrots and celery for the last 40 minutes, then pull the bay leaves and correct the salt.

name: Irish Dublin Coddle Sausage and Potatoes
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 1.5 lb (635 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the bacon into thick pieces and cook it in a large dutch oven until it renders and crisps at the edges.
Cut the bratwurst into thick chunks and brown them lightly in the bacon fat, which is optional in the traditional version but adds a lot.
Add the sliced yellow onions and garlic and cook until they soften and pick up the fat.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into large chunks, then layer them over the meat and onions.
Pour in the chicken broth so it comes about two thirds of the way up, and season with salt, black pepper, dried thyme, and dried parsley.
Cover and cook low, either on the stovetop or in a moderate oven, until the potatoes are completely tender and the broth has turned cloudy and rich.
Uncover for the last stretch if you want the top layer to color, then taste and adjust the salt.

name: Italian Sausage Minestrone
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 8.75 oz dry (245 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the celery and onion, mince the garlic, drain and quarter the artichoke hearts, and drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and brown the hot Italian sausage in crumbles until it takes on color.
Add the celery and onion and cook until they soften, then add the garlic and the dried oregano for a minute.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and the beef broth, season with salt and black pepper, and bring it up to a simmer.
Add the green beans, the artichoke hearts and the chickpeas and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the pasta shells and cook only until they are just tender. Overcooked pasta turns to paste after a night in the fridge, and this soup is meant to be reheated.
Fold in the chopped fresh basil off the heat and stir the parmesan through right before you portion.

name: Izmir Kofte Turkey Meatball and Potato Bake
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Grate or finely mince the onion, then mix it with the ground turkey, bread crumbs, eggs, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Work it just until it holds together and no further.
Roll the mixture into small oval kofte, about the size of your thumb, and set them on a sheet pan.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into thick slices, then toss them with the vegetable oil and a pinch of salt. Spread them on a second sheet pan.
Roast the kofte and the potatoes at 400F for about 20 minutes, until the meat is browned and cooked through to 165F and the potato edges are starting to color.

While those roast, build the sauce: warm the olive oil in a pot, soften the sliced garlic and bell peppers for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste for a minute, then add the crushed and diced tomatoes with salt and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes.
Layer the potatoes and kofte in your baking pans, pour the sauce over everything, and bake at 375F for 30 to 35 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and thick.
Let it sit 10 minutes before you touch it, then transfer the whole bake into your weighed pot and stir gently so every scoop gets sauce.

name: Jamaican Brown Stew Chicken
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4 lb (1848 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken into large pieces and season it with the black pepper, dried thyme, paprika, salt, grated ginger, minced garlic and half the sliced green onions. Let it sit at least 30 minutes.

Heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high, sprinkle in the brown sugar, and let it melt and darken to the color of strong coffee. Do not walk away; the window between browned and burnt is about twenty seconds.
Add the chicken in batches and turn it in the dark sugar until every piece is coated and seared. Set it aside as it browns.
Cook the diced onion and sliced green bell pepper in the same pot for 5 minutes, scraping the bottom to lift the caramel.
Stir in the ketchup, worcestershire sauce and hot sauce, pour in the chicken broth, and bring it to a simmer.

Return the chicken with all its juices, cover, and simmer 30 to 35 minutes until the gravy thickens and the chicken reads 165F. Keep it at a gentle simmer, and the thighs will stay tender and forgiving through the whole cook.
While it simmers, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes, then fold the rice through the stew with the rest of the green onions.

name: Japanese Ginger Pork Shogayaki Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Firm the pork loin in the freezer for about thirty minutes, then slice it as thin as you can against the grain.
Grate the ginger and whisk it with the soy sauce, mirin, chicken broth, and sugar to make the ginger sauce.
Toss the pork slices in a light coating of the all-purpose flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the sliced yellow onions until they soften and start to color, then set them aside.
Cook the pork in batches in a single layer, about a minute per side, until just browned. Crowding the pan is what turns this into a steamed gray mess.
Return all the pork and the onions to the pan, pour in the ginger sauce, and let it bubble until it thickens and coats everything.
Cook the rice according to the package and season the pork with salt and black pepper to taste.

name: Japanese Ground Beef Curry
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in your biggest pot. Brown the ground beef, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the diced onion, carrots, and potatoes and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the flour, curry powder, and garam masala and stir 2 minutes so the raw flour cooks out and the spices toast.
Slowly stir in the beef broth, then the soy sauce and Worcestershire. Simmer uncovered 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the curry thickens to a gravy.
Stir in the peas, simmer 3 minutes, and season with salt and pepper.
Portion rice into 14 containers and ladle the curry over.

name: Japanese Pork Katsu Curry Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Pound the pork chops to about half an inch thick and season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Set up a breading line: flour in one dish, beaten eggs in the next, bread crumbs in the third. Coat each chop flour, then egg, then crumbs, pressing so the crust sticks.
Shallow fry in the vegetable oil over medium-high heat, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and 145F inside. Rest on a rack so the crust stays crisp.
Make the curry sauce: bring water to a simmer per the roux package, drop in the curry roux blocks, and stir until dissolved and thick.
Slice the cutlets into strips, portion rice into 14 containers, lay the katsu on top, and ladle the curry alongside so the crust is not swimming in it.

name: Japanese Pork Nikujaga Potato Stew
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Freeze the pork loin briefly, then slice it as thin as you can manage against the grain.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pot and cook the pork over medium-high heat just until it loses its pink, then push it to the side.
Add the sliced yellow onions and cook until they turn translucent.
Cut the potatoes into large chunks and the carrots on a diagonal, and add both to the pot.
Pour in the chicken broth, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar, and bring it up to a simmer.
Lay a lid or a round of parchment directly on the surface, drop the heat to low, and simmer until the potatoes are tender all the way through but not falling apart.
Add the snow peas in the last two minutes so they stay bright, then season with salt and black pepper to taste.
